description: Hand-written pairs of the same claim: a vague version a reader could take more than one way, and a precise rewrite that pins one reading down. Used to measure the ambiguity checker: it should flag `vague` and leave `precise` alone. `readings` documents what makes the vague version ambiguous.

pairs.vague: Our method significantly improves accuracy over prior work.
pairs.precise: Our method raises top-1 accuracy on ImageNet from 76.1% to 78.3% over ResNet-50 (paired t-test, p < 0.01).

pairs.vague: The model is robust and generalizes well.
pairs.precise: Accuracy drops by at most 2 points under the 15 corruption types of ImageNet-C at severity 3.

pairs.vague: We normalize the features and remove outliers before training. This improves stability.
pairs.precise: We normalize the features and remove outliers before training. Removing outliers alone reduces the variance of the final loss across 5 seeds by half.

pairs.vague: We evaluate on several standard benchmarks.
pairs.precise: We evaluate on GLUE, SuperGLUE, and SQuAD 2.0.

pairs.vague: The proposed algorithm is efficient.
pairs.precise: The proposed algorithm runs in O(n log n) time and processes 1M records in 3 seconds on one CPU core.

pairs.vague: Sleep duration is associated with exam performance.
pairs.precise: Students who slept more than 7 hours scored 6 points higher on average (Pearson r = 0.31); we make no causal claim.

pairs.vague: Our approach outperforms the baselines.
pairs.precise: Our approach achieves a higher F1 than each of the three baselines in Table 2 on all five datasets.

pairs.vague: Attention plays a key role in the model's success.
pairs.precise: Removing the attention layers reduces BLEU from 27.3 to 19.8, the largest drop of any ablation in Table 4.
readings: it is one of several factors

pairs.vague: Most participants preferred the new interface.
pairs.precise: Of the 40 participants, 31 preferred the new interface in the exit survey.

pairs.vague: The second estimator has lower error.
pairs.precise: The second estimator has lower mean squared error than the first on all 1,000 simulated datasets.

pairs.vague: The system works in real-world settings.
pairs.precise: We deployed the system in two hospitals for six months, where it triaged 12,400 radiology reports.

pairs.vague: The encoder feeds the decoder through a bottleneck layer. It can be pruned without loss.
pairs.precise: The encoder feeds the decoder through a bottleneck layer. The bottleneck layer can be pruned to half its width without loss in validation accuracy.

pairs.vague: The method achieves state-of-the-art results.
pairs.precise: The method achieves the best published accuracy on the CIFAR-10 test set among models under 10M parameters, as of March 2026.

pairs.vague: We leverage pretrained embeddings.
pairs.precise: We initialize the input layer with frozen GloVe 300-d embeddings.

pairs.vague: Performance is slightly worse on long documents.
pairs.precise: On documents longer than 4,000 tokens, accuracy is 1.2 points lower than on shorter documents.

pairs.vague: The pipeline handles missing data.
pairs.precise: The pipeline imputes missing numeric values with the column median and drops rows with a missing label.

pairs.vague: Training is faster with the new optimizer.
pairs.precise: With the new optimizer, training reaches 90% validation accuracy in 12 epochs instead of 20, at the same cost per epoch.

pairs.vague: The resulting model is interpretable.
pairs.precise: The resulting model is a decision tree of depth 4, so each prediction can be traced to at most four feature thresholds.

pairs.vague: Label noise affects the classifier.
pairs.precise: With 20% of labels flipped uniformly at random, the classifier's test accuracy falls from 91% to 84%.

pairs.vague: We also observe gains on the held-out set and on the ablations. These results suggest the gains are not due to tuning.
pairs.precise: We also observe gains on the held-out set and on the ablations. Because the held-out set was never used for tuning, the held-out gains suggest the improvements are not due to tuning.
readings: the held-out gains support the claim
the ablation gains support the claim
